plan.split_name: 4-Day Upper/Lower (Upper A / Lower A / Upper B / Lower B), each muscle ~2x/week

days.label: Upper A — Horizontal-Emphasis (Push-bias) + programmed shoulder-health block
days.focus: Neutral/front-of-body horizontal pressing and horizontal rowing; lateral + rear delts; biceps/triceps; FIRST of two weekly rotator-cuff + scapular-stability blocks. Strength flavor: one heavier 5-8 rep neutral-grip press as the day's strength anchor, the rest 8-15.
target_muscles: Pectoralis major (mid/sternal, via flat neutral-grip press)
Rotator cuff: infraspinatus + teres minor (external rotation within ROM), supraspinatus/subscapularis (light)

days.label: Lower A — Knee-Dominant (Quad-emphasis)
days.focus: Squat-pattern knee-dominant strength anchor (heavier 5-8), then quad-biased + lengthened hamstring + glute + adductor + calf accessories at 8-15. Gastroc trained knee-EXTENDED (standing), soleus knee-FLEXED (seated). Hip-flexed (reclined/extended-hip) leg extension to bias rectus femoris.
target_muscles: Hamstrings: hip-extensor heads (RDL / hip hinge, long length)
Soleus (SEATED, knee-flexed calf raise — paired here or Lower B)

days.label: Upper B — Vertical-Emphasis (front-of-body) + SECOND shoulder-health block
days.focus: Neutral/front overhead pressing (NO behind-neck, NO ballistic) and FRONT vertical pulling (to-chest pulldown / neutral-grip pull); incline neutral press to add upper-pec angle variety; lateral + rear delt repeat; arms; SECOND weekly rotator-cuff + scapular block. Strength flavor: heavier 5-8 neutral overhead or incline press.
target_muscles: Lateral deltoid (lateral raise repeat — high-priority therapeutic)
Pectoralis major (upper/clavicular, via incline neutral press)
Rotator cuff: infraspinatus/teres minor (external rotation), subscapularis
Serratus anterior + lower trap (scapular upward-rotation control)

days.label: Lower B — Hip-Dominant (Hamstring/Glute-emphasis)
days.focus: Hip-hinge / hip-dominant strength anchor (heavier 5-8 RDL or hip thrust complex) then knee-flexor hamstring (seated/lying curl), glute, adductor, and calf accessories at 8-15. Seated leg curl to bias hip-extensor heads at long length; second calf session covers the head not emphasized in Lower A.
target_muscles: Hamstrings: hip-extensor heads (RDL / hip hinge, long length)
Hamstrings: knee-flexor heads — semitendinosus, BF short head (leg curl)
Gluteus maximus (hip thrust short-length + hinge long-length)
Quadriceps (secondary, via leg press / split squat)
Soleus (SEATED, knee-flexed) or Gastrocnemius (STANDING) — whichever wasn't emphasized Lower A

weekly_volume.muscle: Back/lats (lats, teres major, rhomboids, mid/lower trap)
Rotator cuff + scapular stability (infraspinatus/teres minor/subscapularis + serratus/lower trap)

loading.rep_scheme: Balanced strength+physique distribution grounded in the load/rep continuum (loads load-independent for hypertrophy ~30-85% 1RM at matched effort; 1-6 reps / 80-100% 1RM is the genuine strength zone). Per exercise role: STRENGTH ANCHOR (one main neutral-grip press per upper day + one knee-dominant and one hip-dominant compound on lower days) = 5-8 reps at ~78-85% 1RM. PRIMARY HYPERTROPHY COMPOUNDS (rows, secondary presses, leg press, hinge accessories) = 8-12 reps at ~70-78%. ISOLATION (lateral/rear delts, curls, extensions, calves, leg curl, leg extension) = 10-15 reps, with ~15-20% of total weekly sets pushed to 15-20 reps (light metabolite work) and ~15-20% kept heavier 6-8 — spanning the spectrum per the SBS sweet-spot heuristic. Net mix lands ~60-70% of sets in a personal 6-15 sweet spot, ~15-20% heavier, ~15-20% lighter.
loading.rir_scheme: Effort autoregulated by exercise class and block week. COMPOUND STRENGTH ANCHORS: 3-5 RIR early-block, intensifying to 2-3 RIR late-block (Helms/Robinson — failure on heavy compounds is slightly inferior for strength and triples acute neuromuscular fatigue vs 3 RIR; reserve 0-1 RIR for end-of-block top sets only). PRIMARY HYPERTROPHY COMPOUNDS: 2-3 RIR, last set ~1 RIR. ISOLATION: 1-2 RIR, final set of each isolation exercise taken to 0-1 RIR (cheap place to spend the closer-to-failure hypertrophy premium; mandatory 0-1 RIR on any LIGHT-load high-rep isolation set because motor-unit recruitment is recruitment-late at low loads). Block-level: ramp RIR DOWN from ~4 to ~1 across each 4-5 week accumulation (Martikainen: equal gains at lower average session-RPE), then deload at 3-6 RIR.
loading.rest: Scaled to fatigue of the movement. Heavy compound strength anchors (5-8 rep neutral press, squat, hinge): 3-4 min (up to 5 min on the heaviest top sets) to preserve load/technique — strength is volume-load dependent. Primary hypertrophy compounds (rows, leg press, secondary presses): 2-3 min to preserve hard reps across sets (Schoenfeld 2016: 3 min > 1 min in trained men). Isolation / small single-joint (laterals, curls, extensions, calves, leg curl): 60-120 s. Antagonist supersets (e.g. row + neutral press, leg curl + leg extension): perform back-to-back, then ~90-120 s shared rest — preserves per-exercise volume while cutting session time ~36% (Burke 2025 RCT). Rotator-cuff/scapular work: 45-75 s, low-fatigue, never to grinding failure.

set_structures: exercise.tech.straight-sets (meta-analysis) — DEFAULT for every compound strength anchor and primary hypertrophy compound (neutral-grip presses, rows, front pulldown, squat, RDL, hip thrust, leg press) via double-progression. It is the benchmark structure no other beats at matched volume, has the LOWEST fatigue cost, and best preserves load/technique on the heavy lifts that carry shoulder-safety stakes. ~70% of total weekly sets sit here.

exercise.tech.antagonist-superset (RCT) — deploy on paired NON-COMPETING upper movements (horizontal row + neutral-grip press; rear-delt/face-pull + lateral raise; biceps + triceps) and lower (seated leg curl + reclined leg extension). Volume-equated RCT (Burke 2025) shows identical hypertrophy/strength with ~36% less session time; each muscle rests while its antagonist works so volume is preserved. Chosen for time-efficiency, NOT extra growth, and it conveniently pairs antagonistic scapular pull with pressing each upper day.

exercise.tech.myo-reps (RCT) — on a subset of ISOLATION work (lateral raises, curls, triceps, calves, leg curl) when time-limited. Comparable hypertrophy/strength to straight sets with reduced duration and BETTER recovery/stress perception (Liberty RCT) — moderate fatigue cost, suits the low-systemic-stress isolation lifts where chasing near-failure is cheap. Not used on shoulder-stakes compounds.

exercise.tech.cluster-set (meta-analysis) — optional on the heavy 5-8 rep neutral-grip press strength anchor when a top-end strength bias is wanted. Short intra-set rests MAINTAIN bar velocity/force with LESS fatigue (Davies meta: equal adaptation, less fatigue accumulation); the controlled, non-grinding nature also keeps pressing technique crisp, which protects the unstable shoulder. Low fatigue cost.

exercise.tech.drop-set (meta-analysis) — sparing finisher use on machine/cable ISOLATION only (lateral raise, leg extension, calf, triceps pushdown). Volume-equated equivalence to straight sets — value is TIME-EFFICIENCY (equal growth in ~half-to-third the time), never more muscle; high fatigue cost so capped at 1-2 exercises/week and kept off free-weight/overhead/shoulder-loaded movements.

exercise.tech.reverse-pyramid (expert) — optional on the lower-body strength anchors (squat/hinge): heaviest top set FIRST while fresh, then lighter back-offs. Equivalent growth to straight sets (Angleri/Fonseca) but lets the maximal-tension strength set be performed unfatigued — a time-efficient, autoregulatory loading organization for the strength goal. AVOIDED on overhead/unstable-shoulder pressing where a maximal first set under fatigue-free load is less desirable than warmed-up straight sets.

AVOIDED as inappropriate for this lifter: exercise.tech.agonist-superset-preexhaust (mechanistically refuted — cuts compound load/volume, no activation or growth benefit) and any high-fatigue intensity technique on overhead/dip/behind-the-body movements that would push the shoulder toward failure in compromised positions.
plan.progression: DOUBLE-PROGRESSION + RIR-AUTOREGULATION across a 4-5 week accumulation block then deload, with MEV->MAV volume ramp (Renaissance Periodization landmark system). (1) START each mesocycle near MEV: ~8-12 working sets/muscle/week, effort at ~3-4 RIR (compounds) / ~2 RIR (isolation). (2) DOUBLE PROGRESSION within each exercise's prescribed rep band: keep load fixed and add reps across sessions until you hit the TOP of the band on all sets at target RIR, then add the smallest load increment (note dumbbells cap at 75 lb — once a DB lift maxes out, progress via reps/added sets/tempo/structure) and drop back to the bottom of the band. (3) RAMP VOLUME within the block (MAV zone) by adding ~1-3 sets/week to lagging or priority muscles (lateral delt, rear delt, back, triceps) as recovery allows, climbing 12->~18-20 sets toward MRV; hold a muscle's volume if you cannot match the prior week's performance (an MRV signal). (4) RAMP RIR DOWN within the block: ~4 RIR week 1 to ~1 RIR final week (Martikainen — equal gains at lower session-RPE); final-week isolation sets to 0-1 RIR. (5) DELOAD when performance stalls or fatigue accumulates: cut to MV (~6 sets/muscle) and back effort off to 3-6 RIR for one week (raising RIR removes the fatigue-generating last reps more cheaply than only cutting volume), then restart at MEV. (6) Strength anchors progress primarily via LOAD at the heavy end (5-8 reps), hypertrophy work via the reps-then-load double progression; frequency is fixed at 2x/week per muscle (the established hypertrophy floor and a sufficient strength dose for intermediates), used as the vehicle to keep each session under the ~6-8 quality-set/muscle per-session ceiling.
shoulder_accommodations: RULE 1 — Therapeutic dosing, NOT protective under-dosing: upper-body and shoulder volume is set GENEROUS-but-recoverable (lateral delt 18, rear delt 16, back 18, plus a dedicated 12 sets/week of rotator-cuff + scapular work). Consistent in-ROM upper training resolves his symptoms; sedentariness worsens them. Do NOT cut shoulder volume to 'protect' it — the protection IS the training, performed within available ROM.

RULE 2 — Programmed rotator-cuff + scapular block TWICE weekly (not an afterthought): each Upper day opens or closes with external-rotation work within available ROM (side-lying/cable ER at neutral or slightly-below-neutral abduction), scapular retraction (prone/seated scap rows) and protraction (serratus punches / push-up-plus), and band pull-aparts. ~6 sets/upper day = 12/week. Kept at 1-2 RIR, controlled tempo, never grinding failure.

RULE 3 — NEUTRAL-GRIP / FRONT-OF-BODY pressing only: all presses use a neutral or pronated grip in front of the body (neutral-grip flat press, neutral DB/landmine overhead press, incline neutral press). He presses fine in these patterns. Substitute neutral-grip pulldowns and rows for any wide pronated end-range movement.

RULE 4 — BAN the apprehension position: never load abduction combined with end-range external rotation. This forbids behind-the-neck press AND behind-the-neck pulldown, wide-grip overhead work taken to end-range, and any cue that drives the elbow far behind the torso plane under load.

RULE 5 — NO deep dips and NO end-range stretch under load at the shoulder: dips (if used at all) stay shallow above the apprehension/impingement zone; pressing and flye-type movements stop short of the deep wide-grip stretch (keep range full but PAIN-FREE, not forced past where the joint feels stable). ROM rule: full available ROM, hard stop at the first sign of instability/apprehension.

RULE 6 — CONTROLLED TEMPO, no ballistic/jerky overhead: every overhead and pressing rep is controlled (roughly 2s eccentric, no bouncing, no push-press/jerk). This is why cluster sets (velocity-maintained) and straight sets are favored over ballistic or grind-to-failure structures on shoulder-loaded lifts.

RULE 7 — Intensity techniques stay OFF shoulder-stakes movements: drop sets / myo-reps / rest-pause are restricted to machine/cable isolation; overhead and free-weight pressing never get pushed to 0 RIR in a fatigued, position-compromised state — heavy presses live at 2-4 RIR.

RULE 8 — Balance the shoulder girdle: rear-delt + horizontal-pull volume (rear delt 16, back 18) is kept >= pressing volume so the posterior cuff/scapular retractors are not outpaced by anterior pressing — a structural-balance safeguard for an unstable anterior capsule.

RULE 9 — STOP-AND-REASSESS red flags (program-level kill switch): halt the set and reassess if any occur — a dislocation/subluxation event, sharp pain, a sense of the shoulder slipping/instability, numbness or tingling down the arm, or sudden loss of strength. Dull working-muscle fatigue/pump is expected and fine; joint-line pain or instability is not.
plan.rationale: Aaron is an intermediate training 4 days/week with a dual strength+physique goal and a therapeutic mandate to train the upper body generously within a stable ROM. A 4-day Upper/Lower hits every muscle ~2x/week — the established hypertrophy frequency floor (Schoenfeld 2016, >=2x beats 1x) and a sufficient strength dose for intermediates — while keeping each session under the ~6-8 quality-set/muscle per-session ceiling (Weightology), which is exactly why high weekly upper volume is split across two upper days rather than crammed. Volume is set in the trained 12-20 sets/muscle MAV zone (Baz-Valle 2022; RP MEV->MRV), biased to the generous end for the therapeutic targets: lateral delt 18, rear delt 16, back 18, plus a budgeted 12 sets/week of rotator-cuff + scapular-stability work treated as a programmed priority. Triceps/biceps land ~14 direct (triceps also bank indirect pressing volume per Baz-Valle's >20-total finding). Lower body is split knee-dominant (Lower A) vs hip-dominant (Lower B) so quads, hamstrings (both hip-extensor and knee-flexor heads — seated curl for the lengthened hip-extensor bias, lying/standing for knee-flexors per Maeo), glutes, adductors, gastroc (standing/knee-extended) and soleus (seated/knee-flexed, per Kinoshita) all get distinct, length-appropriate stimulus. Loading follows the continuum honestly: because hypertrophy is load-independent ~30-85% 1RM at matched effort (Lopez/Schoenfeld — the 'heavy load required' and 'failure required' claims are REFUTED), most work sits 8-15 reps at moderate load and moderate effort, while a genuine 5-8 rep strength anchor per session captures the real strength-zone specificity. RIR is autoregulated — heavy compounds at 2-4 RIR (failure is slightly worse for strength and ~triples acute fatigue per Refalo/Robinson), isolation at 0-2 RIR where the closer-to-failure premium is cheap — and ramps down across each block (Martikainen) before a deload to MV. Set-structure choices lean on the corpus's central refutation: NO advanced technique out-grows volume-equated straight sets, so straight sets anchor the shoulder-stakes compounds (lowest fatigue, best load/technique control) and time-efficient structures (antagonist supersets — RCT-backed, ~36% time saved; myo-reps; capped machine drop sets; clusters for velocity-maintained heavy pressing) are deployed only where they buy efficiency or fatigue-management without risking the joint. Every shoulder accommodation is encoded as a hard programming rule: neutral/front pressing only, banned apprehension position (no behind-neck press/pulldown), no deep dips or forced end-range stretch, controlled non-ballistic tempo, intensity techniques kept off shoulder-loaded lifts, posterior-girdle volume >= pressing volume, and a red-flag kill switch — implementing 'the protection IS the training' rather than under-dosing a shoulder that gets worse when undertrained.

weeks.focus: ACCUMULATION ENTRY / re-groove. Open the mesocycle near MEV with full technique focus on the four strength anchors (Upper A neutral-grip flat press, Lower A squat-pattern, Upper B neutral overhead/incline, Lower B RDL/hip-thrust). Strength anchors: heavy 5-8 work but LIGHT effort to bed in bar path and (on the shoulder) confirm the neutral/front-of-body press groove is pain-free through full available ROM. Both programmed rotator-cuff + scapular blocks run from week 1 at full prescribed dose (this is therapeutic baseline, not a ramp variable) — ~6 sets/upper day = 12/week of ER + scap retraction/protraction + band pull-aparts (RULE 2). Structures: straight-sets only this week (exercise.tech.straight-sets) so every load/RIR is a clean reference point for the double-progression that follows; introduce antagonist supersets (exercise.tech.antagonist-superset) on the non-competing upper pairs only once movements feel grooved.
weeks.rir: Compound strength anchors ~4 RIR (RPE 6); primary hypertrophy compounds 3 RIR; isolation 2 RIR. This is the top of the descending-RIR ramp — Martikainen-style block starting near RIR4 (rir, hypertrophy/intermediate: 'Progress RIR DOWN within a block, start ~4 end ~1'). Heavy anchors sit at the high end deliberately: failure on big lifts is slightly inferior for strength and ~triples acute neuromuscular fatigue vs 3 RIR (exercise.claim.17; rir, strength/intermediate 3-5 RIR).
weeks.volume_note: START at MEV, biased to the generous end for the therapeutic upper targets. Roughly: lateral delt ~14, rear delt ~12, back ~14, chest ~11, biceps/triceps ~11 each, quads ~12, hams ~11, glutes ~11, calves ~10, plus the fixed 12 sets/week rotator-cuff+scapular block which does NOT start low — it runs at full dose all block (RULE 1: therapeutic, not protective under-dosing). Lower-body and arms enter at the bottom of their landmark range (volume_training_variables MEV ~8-12); the shoulder-health and lateral/rear-delt work enter higher because their MEV is effectively their working dose.

weeks.focus: ACCUMULATION — first double-progression step. On every exercise, attempt the top of its prescribed rep band at the same load as week 1 before adding the smallest increment (DB lifts cap at 75 lb — once maxed, progress via reps/added sets/tempo, never grip-width creep on the shoulder). Strength anchors begin loading at the heavy 5-8 end. Add the first MAV sets to the PRIORITY/lagging muscles per the architect's bias — lateral delt, rear delt, back, triceps — not to lower body. Antagonist supersets (exercise.tech.antagonist-superset) now standard on horizontal-row+neutral-press, rear-delt/face-pull+lateral-raise, biceps+triceps, and seated-leg-curl+reclined-leg-extension (Burke 2025 RCT — same growth, ~36% less session time; chosen for efficiency, and it conveniently pairs scapular pull against every press).
weeks.rir: Anchors ~3-4 RIR; primary hypertrophy compounds 2-3 RIR; isolation 1-2 RIR with the LAST set of each isolation exercise to 0-1 RIR (cheap hypertrophy premium where systemic fatigue is low — rir, hypertrophy/intermediate 0-2 RIR isolation). Any LIGHT-load high-rep isolation set must hit 0-1 RIR because motor-unit recruitment is recruitment-late at low loads (rir, hypertrophy/general 0-1 RIR light load; exercise.claim.19).
weeks.volume_note: RAMP +1-3 sets into priority muscles only (RP MAV zone, volume_training_variables MAV 12-20). Target this week ~ lateral delt 16, rear delt 14, back 16, triceps 12; hold lower body and chest where they are. Rotator-cuff/scapular block stays fixed at 12 (it is a constant, never a ramp lever). Stay inside the 12-20 trained optimum (exercise.claim.14, exercise.claim.15: diminishing returns past ~20, so climb deliberately, not greedily).

weeks.focus: ACCUMULATION peak / push toward MAV. Continue double progression — most exercises should now be adding load or sitting mid-band having added load last week. Bring the remaining muscles up to their target weekly volume (lower body, chest, biceps reach the upper-middle of their range). Introduce time-efficient intensity structures ONLY on machine/cable isolation: myo-reps (exercise.tech.myo-reps) or a single capped drop-set (exercise.tech.drop-set) on lateral raise / leg extension / calf / triceps pushdown — equal growth, less time, and explicitly kept OFF every shoulder-loaded and free-weight lift (shoulder RULE 7). Optional: cluster sets (exercise.tech.cluster-set) on the heavy neutral-grip press anchor if a top-end strength bias is wanted — velocity-maintained, lower fatigue, keeps pressing technique crisp on the unstable shoulder.
weeks.rir: Anchors ~3 RIR; primary hypertrophy compounds ~2 RIR, last set ~1; isolation 1 RIR, final sets to 0-1 (and 0 RIR on light-load high-rep finishers). RIR continuing its descent toward the late-block target.
weeks.volume_note: Near-top of the MAV climb: lateral delt ~18, rear delt ~16, back ~18 (the architect's generous therapeutic ceilings), chest ~13-14, quads ~14-15, hams ~13-14, glutes ~13-14, arms ~13-14, calves ~12. This brushes the upper end of the 12-20 optimum where returns diminish (exercise.claim.14/15) — do NOT exceed these absent a clear MRV signal of headroom. Rotator-cuff/scapular work remains pinned at 12.

weeks.focus: INTENSIFICATION — effort over added volume. Volume HOLDS at the week-3 ceiling (you do not keep stacking sets indefinitely — past ~20/muscle the data thin and fatigue dominates, exercise.claim.15); the progression lever shifts to LOAD on the strength anchors and to proximity-to-failure on hypertrophy work. This is where the genuine 5-8 rep strength zone gets expressed: anchors push load at the heavy end, optionally via reverse-pyramid on the LOWER-body anchors only (exercise.tech.reverse-pyramid — heaviest top set first while fresh; explicitly AVOIDED on overhead/unstable-shoulder pressing where a warmed-up straight-set ramp is safer). Watch for MRV signals (can't match prior week's reps/load at adequate rest) and hold any muscle that flags one.
weeks.rir: Anchors ~2-3 RIR (reserve 0-1 RIR for an end-of-block top set only, and only on the lower-body/neutral-press lifts that don't compromise the joint); primary hypertrophy compounds ~1-2 RIR, last set to failure-adjacent; isolation 0-1 RIR throughout. Periodization caveat: the value here is fatigue management and peak-intensity exposure, NOT a matched-volume magic — periodization's edge over a constant program at truly matched volume+intensity is disputed (exercise.claim.21), so this block is structured variation for autoregulation, not because variation itself out-grows.
weeks.volume_note: HOLD volume at week-3 levels for every muscle; redirect adaptation pressure into intensity (load + RIR), not more sets. If any muscle missed performance vs week 3, drop IT back ~2-3 sets while leaving the others — never a blanket cut. Critically: if fatigue forces a trim, the rotator-cuff/scapular block and lateral/rear-delt therapeutic volume are the LAST things touched (RULE 1).

weeks.focus: INTENSIFICATION peak (optional 5th week — run it if recovery is still tracking; collapse to a 4-week block + deload if performance already stalled in week 4). Final realization of the block: top-end loads on the four anchors at their lowest planned RIR, hypertrophy work at peak proximity. No new structures introduced — this is an expression week, so the shoulder-stakes lifts stay on plain straight-sets/clusters (exercise.tech.straight-sets / exercise.tech.cluster-set) at controlled non-ballistic tempo (RULE 6). End-of-block top sets are the ONLY place 0-1 RIR is permitted on a heavy press, and even then only the neutral/front patterns Aaron presses pain-free.
weeks.rir: Anchors ~2 RIR (single end-of-block top set may touch 0-1 RIR on safe patterns only); primary hypertrophy compounds ~1 RIR; isolation 0-1 RIR / final sets to failure. This is the bottom of the descending ramp (~RIR1 average) — Martikainen showed this varying RIR4→RIR1 scheme matches constant-RIR1 gains at LOWER average session RPE (rir, hypertrophy/intermediate descending-RIR; exercise.claim.18: 1-3 RIR already captures nearly the full hypertrophy stimulus, so do not grind every set to 0).
weeks.volume_note: Still HELD at the block ceiling (lateral delt ~18, rear delt ~16, back ~18, etc.) — this is a brief touch of MRV to trigger supercompensation, not a new volume PR. Expect this to be the week most muscles finally signal MRV (can't beat prior performance); that signal is the trigger to deload next, not to add sets (volume_training_variables MRV ~18-25, back off when performance drops).

meso.deload: DELOAD WEEK (week 6, after a 5-week block; week 5 after a 4-week block). Purpose: shed the proximity-driven neuromuscular fatigue that accumulated as RIR descended (Refalo data: failure/near-failure leaves a residual ~3% velocity decrement at 24h that compounds across a block; rir, hypertrophy/intermediate deload). TWO LEVERS, RIR FIRST: (1) Raise effort to 3-6 RIR on everything — this is the higher-value, lower-cost lever because it directly removes the fatigue-generating last reps rather than only cutting stimulus (rir, hypertrophy/intermediate 'hold ~3-6 RIR during deload'). (2) Cut volume toward Maintenance Volume (~6 sets/muscle/week) on the high-fatigue, high-systemic-cost work: the heavy lower-body anchors (squat/RDL/hip-thrust) and the heaviest pressing — these are halved or dropped to ~6 sets, loads pulled back ~10-20%, reps kept submaximal, tempo controlled (volume_training_variables MV ~6 sets preserves mass). CRITICAL ASYMMETRY — protect the therapeutic upper-body dose: do NOT cut the upper body to MV uniformly. The rotator-cuff + scapular-stability block stays at or near its full 12 sets/week (it is low-fatigue, never taken to grinding failure, and it is the literal mechanism that resolves Aaron's symptoms — sedentariness worsens them, RULE 1/RULE 2). Lateral- and rear-delt and back work drop only modestly (e.g. to ~8-10 sets) rather than to 6, since this volume is therapeutic and recoverable; the deload removes systemic/joint fatigue from the heavy compounds, not the light shoulder-health work. Keep all movement pain-free and within ROM; the deload is a fatigue flush, not a layoff (avoiding the sedentary state that flares the shoulder). After the deload, RESTART the next mesocycle at MEV with RIR back at ~4 and re-run the ramp. Note the deload is a fatigue-management tool, not an independent growth driver — its job is to let the next block start fresh (exercise.claim.21: variation/periodization buys fatigue management, not matched-volume superiority).
meso.autoregulation:
DAILY/WEEKLY AUTOREGULATION — ordered so upper-body therapeutic volume is the LAST thing cut, never the first.

RED-FLAG KILL SWITCH (overrides everything; RULE 9): STOP the set and reassess immediately on any of — a dislocation/subluxation event, sharp pain, a sense of the shoulder slipping/instability, numbness or tingling down the arm, or sudden loss of strength. These are joint-line/neural signals, categorically different from the dull working-muscle fatigue/pump that is expected and fine. A red flag ends that exercise for the day; it does NOT mean cut the week's upper-body volume.

WHEN THE SHOULDER FEELS TIGHT (but no red flag): This is a CUE TO MODIFY THE MOVEMENT, NOT TO REMOVE VOLUME — because in-ROM upper training is what resolves Aaron's symptoms (RULE 1). In priority order: (1) shrink ROM to the pain-free/stable portion and keep the set; (2) swap the loaded pattern for a friendlier one within the same muscle target — neutral-grip / front-of-body / machine or cable instead of free-weight, landmine instead of straight-bar overhead (RULE 3); (3) slow the tempo and drop the load, keeping 2-3 RIR (RULE 6, no ballistic reps); (4) front-load that day's rotator-cuff + scapular block and band pull-aparts as a 'feeder' to warm and stabilize the joint, then re-attempt the pressing. Only AFTER these fail to settle it do you reduce that single exercise's sets — and you bank the removed sets into the cuff/scap or rear-delt work, keeping the girdle balanced (RULE 8: posterior/horizontal-pull volume kept >= pressing volume).

WHEN RECOVERY IS POOR (bad sleep, high life stress, can't match last session's reps/load at adequate rest = an MRV signal): CUT EFFORT BEFORE VOLUME, AND CUT THE RIGHT VOLUME FIRST. (1) First lever — raise RIR by ~1-2 across the session (e.g. anchors to 3-4 RIR, isolation to 2 RIR); this removes the costly last reps and recovers cheaply (rir descending-block + deload logic; exercise.claim.17/18 — 1-3 RIR already captures nearly all the hypertrophy stimulus, so backing off effort costs almost no growth). (2) Second lever — if still flat, trim sets from the HIGHEST-FATIGUE, HIGHEST-SYSTEMIC-COST work FIRST: the heavy lower-body anchors and the heaviest pressing, and drop the optional intensity techniques (drop-sets/myo-reps, exercise.tech.drop-set/exercise.tech.myo-reps) before anything else. (3) PROTECTED LAST — the rotator-cuff/scapular block, lateral/rear-delt, and back volume are the final things touched; the cuff/scap block is effectively never cut on a bad week because it is low-fatigue and therapeutic (RULE 1/RULE 2). Rationale: a bad week is exactly when the sedentary-flare risk is highest, so the upper-body dose that keeps the shoulder healthy must survive.

WHEN PERFORMANCE STALLS ACROSS A WHOLE MUSCLE for 2+ sessions despite rest: that muscle has hit MRV — hold or shave 2-3 sets from THAT muscle only (not a blanket cut), or trigger the deload if multiple muscles flag together (volume_training_variables MRV — back off when you can't match prior performance). Hold the muscle's volume rather than forcing more sets into a non-recovering tissue.

DEFAULT STRUCTURE BIAS UNDER FATIGUE: when time or recovery is short, keep the shoulder-stakes compounds on plain straight-sets (exercise.tech.straight-sets — lowest fatigue cost, best load/technique control, and the structure no advanced technique out-grows at matched volume, exercise.claim.13/17) and shed the time-saving structures rather than the safe ones.
